A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCP-based causal-discovery study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. V4's appendices A–H are retained and expanded in v5, which also adds appendices I and J.

before.justification: V4 reports original benchmark evaluations, health-screening experiments, SCP simulations, uncertainty analyses, and comparisons across GPT models.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds downstream graph-stability simulations, open-source LLM evaluations, and prompt-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The four-step procedure, Algorithms 1–3, adopted prompt templates, and 0.05/0.95 thresholds are retained. Appendix I documents selection of existing wording; Appendix J discusses a possible alternative application of the probability matrix without changing the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Auto MPG, DWD climate, Sachs protein, and health-screening coverage is retained. Appendix I adds six causal-direction questions involving hour of day, temperature, and electricity load, using Tübingen-derived ground truths. This is additional question-level evaluation, rather than a new full numerical-data SCD benchmark.

E2.justification: Appendix I adds an explicit comparison of direct zero-shot question answering with generated-knowledge prompting and evaluates alternative question templates against the selected wording. The main no-prior-knowledge and Pattern 0 baselines, and the PC, Exact Search, and DirectLiNGAM comparisons, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V5 adds distinct protocols for open-source LLM configurations, a 20-template accuracy evaluation with and without generated knowledge, and independent Gaussian perturbations of probability matrices followed by DirectLiNGAM. Existing main-experiment settings are retained. The Qwen configuration is ambiguous: Appendix H.2 specifies 32B, whereas Table 19 and Section 3.1 specify 7B.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5 newly tests whether uncertainty in LLM probabilities propagates into final graph edges and coefficients, using DWD and DirectLiNGAM Pattern 2. Appendix I adds systematic prompt-wording sensitivity experiments under two prompting conditions. These substantially extend the retained coefficient/bootstrap-prompt simulations and token-probability analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix D.5 adds uncertainty propagation using 10,000 simulated probability matrices and coefficient histograms. Appendix I reports 50 repetitions per question. The existing five probability measurements, 1,000 bootstrap resamplings, standard-error analyses, and regression reporting are retained; the new counts do not represent increased repetitions of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Substantial supplementary results are added while existing numerical results remain unchanged. Table 19 reports DWD Pattern 0 SHD values of 4 for Llama and 6 for Gemma, versus 10 without prior knowledge. Tables 23 and 27 report Q4 accuracy of 0.67 under zero-shot prompting and 0.83 with generated knowledge. Figure 18 adds evidence of narrowly concentrated causal coefficients under simulated probability perturbations.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a runtime decomposition and pairwise LLM-cost derivation in Equations 1–5. Appendix J adds mathematical discussion distinguishing token probabilities from interventional probabilities and considers an edge-probability graph likelihood. Existing mathematical definitions and derivations are retained. The new complexity equations inconsistently use N after defining n as the number of variables.

C1.justification: The central claims about integrating LLM-KBCI with SCD and benefiting from SCP remain. V5 narrows the health-screening claims by describing possible rather than established dataset biases and replacing 'robustly leads' with 'can lead' in Section 1.3. Merging overlapping contribution bullets does not remove the SCP-improvement claim.

C2.justification: V5 substantially expands qualifications concerning proof of training-data non-overlap in Appendix C.4 and the inability to directly use LLM confidence probabilities for causal-effect estimation in Appendix J. It adds explanations for downstream graph stability in D.5 and a stronger privacy argument based on withholding raw records. H.2 also attributes support to SCP despite Table 19 evaluating Pattern 0 without SCP.

D1.justification: V5 newly specifies Fisher's Z test for PC and BIC scoring for Exact Search, supplies the prompt alternatives and generated knowledge used in Appendix I, and clarifies health-data provenance and handling. These additions improve documentation without establishing changed settings for retained experiments. Code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: New references support prompt sensitivity, training-data contamination detection, LLM ensembles, open-source models, and uncertain causal graphs. The main related-work positioning remains largely intact. The Kiciman reference changes from its preprint to its published version and is not a newly cited work.

P1.justification: V5 makes distributed language and terminology corrections, adds section roadmaps and explanatory subheadings, and merges overlapping contribution bullets. Appendix H gains subsections, the old D.5 becomes D.6, and appendices I–J are added. Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: V5 adds a substantial set of displays: graph-stability histograms in Figure 18, the question benchmark graph in Figure 19, and Tables 19–27 covering models, prompts, knowledge inputs, and accuracy results. Table 3 is reorganized into separately annotated dataset blocks, with bold highlighting replacing blue text; Table 18 uses underlining. Existing result figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new stability and prompt-selection studies, non-GPT checks, and explicit limits on proving training-data non-overlap make the unchanged method easier to assess. The gain is limited by the narrow new tests, the Qwen 7B/32B inconsistency, and Appendix H.2's attribution of no-SCP Pattern 0 results to SCP. These additions improve supporting evidence and transparency without substantially resolving the retained reliability limitations.
